messages:
anya: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak merged yesterday, we're seeing a steady uptick in tail OOMs on AWQ + FP8 runs when KV cache dtype is float16. Landing around 2-3% failure rate on canary traffic.
jon: ugh. which switch? the heuristic that prefers fp32 kernels for certain aten ops?
anya: yeah. the kernel-rank change that biases for numerically stable kernels under 512 seq. It looks like those kernels allocate a bigger temp workspace.
lee: can you paste the profiler snapshot? small logs help.
anya: pasted a lightweight trace: ```
# profiler excerpt
op conv_attn: chosen_kernel=fp32_fused_attn, temp_work=42MB
op kv_cache_pack: dtype=float16, stage=temp_copies, temp_work=18MB
op matmul: chosen_kernel=fp8_gemm_opt, temp_work=12MB
total_workspace_peak: ~1.9GB (expected ~1.6GB)
```
maria: interesting — temp copy for kv_pack + fp32_attn seems additive. fp32 kernel inflates workspace and causes fragmentation.
sam: were these runs using dynamic batching? If batch shapes vary, fragmentation makes peaks worse.
anya: yes, observed on dynamic batch hinting enabled in canary. Static batch tests are fine.
jon: could be two problems: kernel selection favors fp32 which uses a bigger workspace, and workspace allocator's reuse window is too aggressive (not reusing across short-lived allocations).
lee: quick mitigation: force kernel selector to prefer fp8-compatible kernels for canary (unsafe but quick) and bump allocator soft_reserve by 200MB. Can we try a canary patch?
anya: started a canary with kernel-override flag, +200MB reserve. deploy-bot: canary deploy started: infra/canary/slot-7 -> 1958765460.
anya: early signs look better: OOMs down to 0.6%. But latency p99 increased ~4ms.
maria: tradeoff expected. Longer term we should: 1) refine kernel cost model to include temp_work footprint, 2) update batching heuristic to align similar seq-lengths, 3) make KV cache dtype conversion lazy to avoid copies.
jon: + add a workspace-simulator in CI to catch these regressions. We can simulate allocation patterns from trace logs and compute peak fragmentation overhead.
sam: I prototyped a small sim that replays malloc/free events with slab pooling heuristics. Found that our reuse window of 10ms causes a missed coalescing for staggered MACs. Moving to a size-aware LRU within the window reduced peak by ~120MB.
lee: nice. can you open PR with sim + unit tests on a few real traces? Put the AWQ+fp8 KV-case as regression test.
sam: on it. PR will include a toggle to switch allocator policy and a small benchmark harness.
anya: also flag: KV cache dtype mismatch. The cache is stored as float16 but sometimes kernels expect fp32 temporaries, so we copy up then back down. We should: a) let kernels accept view-casts when safe, or b) stage conv buffers in fp32 only when necessary.
maria: agree. add typing metadata to the KV entries (stored_dtype, usage_hotness) so we can lazily upcast only hot keys.
jon: for immediate relief, add an allocator fastpath that tries to satisfy temp_work from a transient pool that doesn't fragment the main heap (evict quickly). That reduces long-term fragmentation.
lee: +1. infra-bot: scheduled a follow-up sync Thu 10:00 to align on milestones: kernel-cost-model, allocator-sim PR, KV dtype metadata.
anya: next steps: sam -> PR for allocator sim and policy, jon -> kernel selector weight fix, maria -> KV dtype prototype, lee -> watch canary and rollback if p99 latency > +10ms or OOMs > 1%.
omm-bot: (system) OOM alert suppression lifted — alerts will resume after canary stabilized.
deploy-bot: canary deploy health: 1958765460 -> healthy: 92%, OOM rate: 0.6%, p99 +4ms.
anya: thanks all — let's keep short updates in this thread.
